title: Inconsistent and underdocumented behavior when choosing a digest
body:
In various locations, notably user-visible “inspect” operations, we expose a _single_ digest value for an image.

That’s fundamentally insufficient because images are deduplicated; hence `libimage.Image.Digest` has a TODO to deprecate, but we can’t completely remove it, the `inspect` CLI operations would still need to output _something_.

What exactly we output is not generally consistent, though. Three notable origins of data:
- Raw c/storage access; e.g. `storageTransport.GetStoreImage(…).Digest` . The `c/storage.Image.Digest` value is typically, by c/image, set when the image is _first_ created; and if it was pulled from a multi-arch image, it is the multi-arch digest.
- `c/image/storageReference.resolveReference`, e.g. `storageTransport.ResolveReference().Digest` for a tagged reference or a storage ID. The value used is `BigDataDigests[storage.ImageDigestBigDataKey]`, set on the _last_ write of a duplicate image, and if that was a multi-arch image pull, it is the per-arch digest.
- (User input: `storageTransport.ResolveReference().Digest` when the input reference is a name@digest reference.)

The practical outcome is that `podman image list` currently returns `Image.Digest` values, but things like `podman image inspect` or `podman container inspect` return `BigDataDigests[storage.ImageDigestBigDataKey]` — and the two don’t match. That’s, at the very least, counterintuitive.

---

Fixing this should probably ensure that `libimage` consistently returns one of the values — and given the need to respect user input, probably the one from `c/image/storageReference.resolveReference` (but it _is_ an option to change the implementation of that function).

But, also, that work should probably holistically include how multi-arch/per-arch digests are chosen/treated, notably https://github.com/containers/common/blob/4b53eca53c7a03b98161ae1727f4196517f5fcbc/libimage/manifest_list.go#L201-L205 , https://github.com/containers/common/blob/4b53eca53c7a03b98161ae1727f4196517f5fcbc/libimage/runtime.go#L360-L362 and the like.

comments.body:
A design question: If the user pulls several per-arch variants of the same multi-arch image, should the “digest” field in `podman image list` be the same for all variants (the multi-arch manifest)? Or different for all variants (the per-arch manifest)?

Either can be argued to be correct.

> @vrothberg PTAL

I've no time to work on this in case that's the expectation.

> If the user pulls several per-arch variants of the same multi-arch image, should the “digest” field in podman image list be the same for all variants (the multi-arch manifest)? Or different for all variants (the per-arch manifest)?

Purely by a gut feeling:  I'd vote for individual digest over common list digest.  Maybe even differentiate between list digest and individual digest long term?  `podman image inspect` could display the two in separate fields.

This was motivated by a failure vendoring c/common due to a behavior change. Short-term we adjusted the test, and it is not urgent.

This issue is filed
- to record the situation as (with some effort) determined
- to track fixing it; doing that consistently throughout the codebase might be a bit of an effort, and the design is unclear ATM
- possibly to have a place to point users to; the change in digest values will be user-visible (for users who care at this level of detail) in Podman 5.0, so if it turned out to be hugely disruptive, having a single issue to track should help.

This problem still occurs on podman 5.8.7. I want to agree on a design before I send a PR.

**Reproducer**

```bash
skopeo copy docker://quay.io/libpod/alpine:latest oci:./a:gz --override-arch amd64 --dest-compress-format gzip
skopeo copy oci:./a:gz oci:./b:zst --dest-compress-format zstd
podman pull oci:./a:gz && podman tag <id> localhost/t:a
podman pull oci:./b:zst && podman tag <id> localhost/t:b
```

Both pulls give the same image ID, because both manifests have the same config.

| Name | Manifest | `images --digests` | `inspect .Digest` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `t:a` | `287627ba…` | `287627ba…` | `723aea09…` (wrong) |
| `t:b` | `723aea09…` | `287627ba…` (wrong) | `723aea09…` |

`RepoDigests()` pairs each name with each digest of the image. Some pairs never existed.

**Why not `repo@digest` in `Names`**

podman#3761 ([comment](https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/3761#issuecomment-520180830)) and #175 suggest this. I tried it. It causes these problems:

- `rmi repo:tag` removes only the tag. The image stays, because it has more names.
- `rmi <id>` without `--force` fails with "more than one tag".
- An old image keeps `repo@<old digest>` after a new pull. Because it is never dangling, `image prune` does not remove it.
- `AddNames` puts each new name first in `NamesHistory`. `podman ps --external` and `container runlabel` use `NamesHistory[0]`, so they show a digest, not the tag.
- `podman images` copies `Names` to `RepoTags`. Each pull shows a digest as a tag.
- `Names` is a set. It cannot show which digest came with which tag. #218 needs this link.

**Proposal**

1. c/storage: add a record to `Image`.
   - Field `name-digests` in `images.json`: name → manifest digests of the last pull with that name.
   - New store method `AddNameWithDigests(id, name, digests)`. It adds the name and replaces its record under the `AddNames` lock.
   - It accepts only digests in `Image.Digests`.
   - When a name leaves an image, its record goes too.
   - `Names` and `NamesHistory` do not change.
2. c/image: on commit, record the per-platform digest. If the top-level manifest is a list, also record the list digest.
   - c/image finds the method through an optional interface.
   - If the store does not have it, c/image calls `AddNames` as before.
3. c/common: `RepoDigests()` uses the record of each name.
   - `repo@digest` without a record: its own digest.
   - Tag without a record: the current pairing. Exception: the repository has a `repo@digest` name.

Results:

- The multi-arch tests in `test/e2e/pull_test.go` must give the same output. I will run them before the PR.
- `Image.Digest()` and `images --digests` do not change. They keep the first digest, because a lookup by ID has no name.
- A later PR can use the record for #218.

**Questions**

1. An older c/storage drops `name-digests` when it writes `images.json`. Those names then use the current pairing again. This occurs on hosts that share storage between versions, for example Podman and an older CRI-O. Is this acceptable?
   - I did not use `Flags`. Old writers keep `Flags`, but they do not update it when a tag moves. The result can be a wrong digest.
2. Do you prefer an optional interface or a new `storage.Store` method? A new method stops the compilation of external `Store` implementations and mocks.
3. Old images have no record. Example: `repo@A` from a pull by digest, and `repo:tag` from a pull that brought manifest B.
   - Today `RepoDigests()` shows `repo@A` and `repo@B`.
   - With this change, it shows only `repo@A` until the next pull.
   - A lookup by `repo@B` still works.
   - Is this acceptable?

If you agree, I can send one PR to container-libs with the three parts.

> This problem still occurs on podman 5.8.7. I want to agree on a design before I send a PR.

These things are tricky enough that it’s a bit difficult to commit to a design before seeing it fully work… and, to be fair to you, our capacity to review larger changes is currently constrained; hopefully it will get better in a few weeks/months.

> **Reproducer**
> 
> skopeo copy docker://quay.io/libpod/alpine:latest oci:./a:gz --override-arch amd64 --dest-compress-format gzip
> skopeo copy oci:./a:gz oci:./b:zst --dest-compress-format zstd
> podman pull oci:./a:gz && podman tag <id> localhost/t:a
> podman pull oci:./b:zst && podman tag <id> localhost/t:b

The `podman tag <id>` operations give up on maintaining any kind of association of the tag with a pulled manifest; while that might be a way to easily reproduce the current situation, it’s _not_ really a representative test case of what `podman pull` does.

---

> **Why not `repo@digest` in `Names`**
> 
> * `rmi repo:tag` removes only the tag. The image stays, because it has more names.
> * `rmi <id>` without `--force` fails with "more than one tag".

ACK, the repo:tag -> digest mapping needs to be “weak references”.

---

> **Proposal**
> 
> 1. c/storage: add a record to `Image`.
>    
>    * Field `name-digests` in `images.json`: name → manifest digests of the last pull with that name.

At a glance, a top-level field surprises me a bit; these look like per-image values. A specific concern to think about is that name updates of `repo:latest` on pull should be atomic, there should never be a time when `repo:latest` does not resolve (and there should never be a time when a matching `repo:latest` is missing from `RepoDigests`) — and currently name updates and image creation / data updates are two separate steps, especially when the image ID already exists locally.

Also, a single on-registry manifests digest can exist in multiple local image IDs. That can clearly happen, and must be supported, for multi-platform images (one ID per platform) which share the top-level manifest digest; and in that case `RepoDigests` of each per-platform image should report the right values [whatever that means]. If we had a single shared “name → all possible digests” map, we would then need to filter it for each image ID to see which manifests actually exist there.

>    * New store method `AddNameWithDigests(id, name, digests)`. It adds the name and replaces its record under the `AddNames` lock.

If we are adding a new method, it should be specific to images to avoid the irrelevant layer/container naming lookups and locking.

> * It accepts only digests in Image.Digests.

See above about multiple image IDs sharing a top-level manifest, but not sharing the per-platform manifest; doing that with a top-level map, not specific to individual images, would be non-obvious.

>    * When a name leaves an image, its record goes too.

Probably not, or not _entirely_? For RepoDigests to be exact, after
```sh
podman pull repo:latest // digestA
podman pull repo:latest // digestB
```
we want the image with `digestA` to report `repo@digestA` in RepoDigests.

That suggests that the mapping should not be “name → digests”; maybe “(repo, optionalTag) → digests”. _And_ that the mapping should be deleted when the image is removed, not when the name is removed/moved (although we might need an update when the name is moved).

> 2. c/image: on commit, record the per-platform digest. If the top-level manifest is a list, also record the list digest.
>    
>    * c/image finds the method through an optional interface.

We don’t need that complexity. A hard dependency on a new-enough c/storage is fine.

> 3. c/common: `RepoDigests()` uses the record of each name.
>    
>    * `repo@digest` without a record: its own digest.
>    * Tag without a record: the current pairing. Exception: the repository has a `repo@digest` name.

I think that we want the current pessimistic “report all digests” values when we don’t have better data.

> * The multi-arch tests in `test/e2e/pull_test.go` must give the same output. I will run them before the PR.

(I did not review them, no opinion.)

> * `Image.Digest()` and `images --digests` do not change. They keep the first digest, because a lookup by ID has no name.

What is the benefit of all of this, then? The report primarily tracks the situation that `podman images --digests` and `podman inspect .Digest` contain unexpected values. Only `RepoDigests`? I mean, that would still be pretty valuable, but we’d want to keep this report open.

---

> **Questions**

One major thing to settle, if the goal is more precise RepoDigests: What should be recorded there for multi-platform images, pulled by a reference to the top-level manifest: Only the top-level manifest? Also the per-platform one? If the latter, we might want some kind of `podman inspect --arch=amd64` vs. `podman inspect --arch=arm64` that return different values. That’s probably more complexity than anyone wants, OTOH then we need to be careful about the _precise_ definition of `RepoDigests`; an image could be located by a digest not included there.

> 1. An older c/storage drops `name-digests` when it writes `images.json`. Those names then use the current pairing again. This occurs on hosts that share storage between versions, for example Podman and an older CRI-O. Is this acceptable?

Yes. Eventually we should think about versioning the store, but that’s ~orthogonal to this work.

> 2. Do you prefer an optional interface or a new `storage.Store` method? A new method stops the compilation of external `Store` implementations and mocks.

New `storage.Store` method is what always happens. (Yes, we should not be exporting that interface at all, because we keep extending it, but that’s for a future ABI break if any.)

> 4. Old images have no record. Example: `repo@A` from a pull by digest, and `repo:tag` from a pull that brought manifest B.>    
>    * Today `RepoDigests()` shows `repo@A` and `repo@B`.
>    * With this change, it shows only `repo@A` until the next pull.
>    * A lookup by `repo@B` still works.
>    * Is this acceptable?

No, see above.

Thank you for your time, and for the full answer. The suggestions help a lot.

I changed the design to follow your points:

- The record is per image. It stays when a pull moves the name to a different image, so the old image still shows `repo@digestA`. It goes away when the image is deleted. An explicit `untag` of that name also removes it.
- A new `storage.Store` method only for images. No optional interface.
- Without a record, `RepoDigests` keeps the current "all digests" values.
- For multi-platform images, the record has the per-platform digest and the list digest. This agrees with the current e2e tests.
- The name move and the record change occur in one `images.json` save, so `repo:latest` always resolves.
- I will test with a pull from a local registry, not with `podman tag`.

The change fixes only `RepoDigests`. `images --digests` and `inspect .Digest` do not change, so the PR will not close this issue.

I will send one PR with the three parts (c/storage, c/image, c/common). It will be a draft, so you can see it work first. It can be a bit large, mostly because of the tests. I understand that review time is limited, and there is no hurry.
